There are major strategic gains in terms of health benefits and savings to government arising] from effective primary and secondary prevention (see Box 4.1 describing these terms).

4.52 Yet the current health system focuses on efforts at curative treatment, often in

hospitals, more so than prevention of diseases in the first place. According to Vanuatu's

National Health Accounts, inpatient curative care absorbed 30 percent of government health

expenditure in 2007; outpatient curative care absorbed a further 32 percent. Prevention and

public health services absorbed 11 percent, and prevention of NCDs absorbed just 2.2 percent of

government expenditure (Government of Vanuatu, 2011b). The Public Expenditure Review

Health 2011 found that combined spending on NCD prevention was only VT 1.6 million, or 0.6

percent of total public health allocation. (Government of Vanuatu, 2012e )

4.53 More recent figures suggest that the allocation to the Public Health Program - the locus

for prevention - has risen slightly in nominal terms in the years between 2006 and 2012 (from

VT 50.7 million to VT 60.2 million) but actually fallen from 4.7 percent of government
